plan.title: Add a read-only `gate` subcommand to the frozen Go binary (deft-install) per #1933 Option 3

narratives.Description: #1933 locked Option 3 on 2026-06-24: the frozen Go binary (deft-install) gains a node-independent read-only health-gate role alongside its existing reshaper role, so consumers run a prebuilt static binary needing no Python and no Go toolchain. This story carves the read-only state-vector probe (`OK v<current>` / `NEEDS-UPGRADE recorded=… current=… precutover=… agents-md=…`, exit 0 healthy / 1 needs-upgrade) into the Go binary, because the bootstrap paradox forbids a Node-engine CLI verb from probing the very engine that may be missing or broken.
narratives.ImplementationPlan:
- Add a `gate` subcommand to the deft-install Go source (a new gate file under cmd/deft-install) that reads the VERSION marker, detects pre-cutover layout, and classifies the AGENTS.md managed-section without writing anything.
- Cover the state-vector output and exit codes (0 healthy, 1 needs-upgrade) with a Go test that asserts each documented vector string.
- Hand off a maintainer-only refreeze: rebuild the static deft-install binary and re-pin the frozen release so the gate ships on the consumer path; the Go build toolchain stays maintainer-only.
narratives.UserStory: As a deft consumer on the npm path, I want a node-independent `gate` probe in the prebuilt binary, so that the bootstrap health check runs even when Node or the engine is missing or broken.

items.title: Given a missing or broken Node engine, when an agent runs the frozen binary's `gate` subcommand, then it returns a state vector and exit code without requiring Node, Python, or a Go toolchain.

narrative.Acceptance: Given a missing or broken Node engine, when an agent runs the frozen binary's `gate` subcommand, then it returns a state vector and exit code without requiring Node, Python, or a Go toolchain.

items.title: Given a healthy install, when `gate` runs, then it shows `OK v<current>` and exits zero; given a stale install, then it shows the NEEDS-UPGRADE vector and exits one.

narrative.Acceptance: Given a healthy install, when `gate` runs, then it shows `OK v<current>` and exits zero; given a stale install, then it shows the NEEDS-UPGRADE vector and exits one.

items.title: Given the locked Option 3 decision, when `gate` runs, then it only reads state and never writes AGENTS.md, migrates, or reshapes the layout.

narrative.Acceptance: Given the locked Option 3 decision, when `gate` runs, then it only reads state and never writes AGENTS.md, migrates, or reshapes the layout.

items.title: Given a refrozen release, when an npm consumer installs, then the deposited prebuilt binary resolves the `gate` subcommand on the consumer path.
